'''Landon Timmonds Ross Jr.''' (October 19, 1942 – February 7, 2016) was an American environmental biologist. He received master's degrees in [[geology]] from [[Florida State University]] ([http://siris-libraries.si.edu/ipac20/ipac.jsp?uri=full=3100001~!187893!0 FSU master's thesis]) and [[paleontology]] ([[Harvard University]]), and a [[biology]] Ph.D. from Florida State ([http://siris-libraries.si.edu/ipac20/ipac.jsp?uri=full=3100001~!908584!0 FSU doctoral dissertation]), while studying [[malacology]] there.

Ross spent his career, between 1970 and 2000, employed as an environmental biologist: as lead biologist with the state of [[Florida]] agency regulating the environment ([[Florida Department of Pollution Control|Pollution Control]], [[Florida Department of Environmental Regulation|Environmental Regulation]]), or as central biology laboratory leader ([[Florida Department of Environmental Protection|Environmental Protection]]). His scientific contributions cover a relatively wide range of subjects, mostly related to Florida's environment.<ref>[https://www.amazon.co.uk/dp/B00071TG02 "An identification guide to the ferns of the Florida Panhandle"]</ref><ref>[https://www.amazon.com/dp/B00072OWGO "The relationship between Jackson turbidity units and nephelometric turbidity units, as determined from various Florida sediment samples"]</ref>
